PullRequest.Title: agentHost: lean tools + CLI-parity prompt for HydraFusion
PullRequest.Body:

Brings HydraFusion cost in the Agent Host in line with Copilot CLI (microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9756).

**Changes**
- Default-exclude 42 VS Code-only tools for `hydrafusion` (59 → 17 tools); user `modelCapabilityOverrides` still win.
- Add CLI tone / search / tool-efficiency prompt sections for `hydrafusion`.
- Artifact `system_reminder`: the agent host doesn't inject one (artifact guidance lives only in the tool description), so excluding `add_artifact_or_reference` already removes it. No change needed.
- `rename_chat` reminder: new sessions use deferred (host-generated) titles, which never inject it. Only restored legacy `activeAgent` sessions do, and the title controller can't see the launcher's per-model tool filters, so that path is left unchanged.

**Results** (TerminalBench 2.1, MSBench, 3 replicas/arm)

| Arm | Resolve | AIC/task | Opus input/req |
|---|---|---|---|
| Control (main) | 77.8% | 74.9 | 44.0K |
| Tools excluded | 78.7% | 60.2 | 29.0K |
| Tools excluded + CLI prompt (this PR) | 81.6% | 56.4 | 27.6K |

- The benchmark excluded all 44 tools; `ask_user`/`web_fetch` are kept here because the interactive CLI ships them.
- AIC vs control: **0.75x** (95% CI 0.67–0.83); vs CLI prod: 1.01x (0.91–1.12). Resolve delta +3.7 pts (n.s.).
- Run IDs: control 2026092980577334, 2026092980578812, 2026092980580219 · tools-excluded 2026092980553243, 2026092980554682, 2026092980556244 · this PR 2026092983442733, 2026092983444192, 2026092983445765 · CLI prod 2026092280637698, 2026092280650597, 63925722795614, 63925724792440, 63925728098446

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: HydraFusion sessions inherited the generic Agent Host tool inventory, so dozens of VS Code-only tool definitions were included in the model's request context instead of the lean CLI-compatible profile.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Each HydraFusion model request carried substantially more serialized tool-schema tokens, increasing request cost and agent interaction consumption.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: On every HydraFusion create/resume without an explicit tool filter, the launcher passes HYDRAFUSION_DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_TOOLS to the SDK, preventing 42 VS Code-only tool schemas from being serialized into repeated model requests while preserving explicit user overrides.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Commit 31671b1f50693b2b9f551f72b519c3afe225990a introduced the selectable HydraFusion model. In the base launcher, absent a user override, excludedTools stayed undefined and the generic runtime registered the full client/server/extension tool set into the SDK session. The changed path now selects a 42-name HydraFusion denylist and forwards it through ResumeSessionConfig.excludedTools. The PR's measured comparison reports HydraFusion request input falling from 44.0K to 27.6K tokens and AIC/task from 74.9 to 56.4, consistent with the code comment identifying roughly 13K tool-definition tokens per request.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume an Agent Host session whose effective model family is HydraFusion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session configuration is built before the SDK createSession/resumeSession RPC can proceed. The changed synchronous model check, fixed denylist selection, and prompt-section assembly are on this path but bounded; existing custom-agent/BYOK/shell preparation remains concurrently awaited. The denylist then reduces tool schemas carried by subsequent model requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate/customize agent and plugin data and optionally read a configured prompt override file while building session configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing work once per create/resume, proportional to configured plugins plus at most one prompt override file; unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same filesystem preparation ran before HydraFusion-specific exclusions and prompt registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before SDK session creation/resumption, but independent preparation is already parallelized.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or resume the SDK session in the Copilot runtime with the assembled config.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One normal-path RPC per launch/resume; existing custom-agent retry and empty-session fallback can add attempts only on their pre-existing error paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create/resume RPC occurred with no HydraFusion default excludedTools list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks session readiness; the diff changes bounded config fields but does not add an RPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send model requests whose context includes the session system prompt and enabled tool definitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or more requests per user turn according to the existing agent loop; no changed fan-out or concurrency. The effective enabled-tool cardinality falls by up to 42 absent an explicit override.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: HydraFusion inherited the generic tool inventory, so the excluded schemas could be carried in each request; this PR removes that repeated payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model request latency/cost is on the turn critical path; the changed denylist reduces repeated serialized tool-schema tokens, while the HydraFusion prompt replacement is bounded.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Costs scale with session launches/resumes and model-request count. Tool-filter work is O(42 plus current client-tool names) once per launch; repeated request payload decreases with the 42 excluded definitions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The launcher still resolves BYOK, shell tools, and custom agents with the existing Promise.all. Exactly one SDK create or resume attempt is made on the normal path; existing resume retry/fallback behavior is unchanged. Model requests remain sequenced by the existing session/agent loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is added or bypassed. Static prompt strings and the fixed denylist live for the module lifetime; per-session config is recomputed on create/resume as before. Explicit availableTools/excludedTools overrides deterministically replace the default.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed denylist is passed directly to ResumeSessionConfig.excludedTools, and prompt resolution occurs once per launch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency savings depend on SDK serialization and request mix, but the reduced enabled-tool cardinality and request-context mechanism are direct. The PR-provided benchmark supports a substantial token reduction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The dominant effect is a bounded session-setup check that removes repeated request serialization/network payload; this concrete regression fix was recorded separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch an existing chat into or out of the exact HydraFusion model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing model change marks the live session for restart when crossing the HydraFusion ID boundary; the next send destroys/resumes before issuing the model request. The resumed configuration applies or removes the new profile.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Set the model, then destroy/resume the SDK session on the next send when crossing the HydraFusion boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one restart per effective boundary crossing before the next send; unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exact HydraFusion transitions already requested the same restart before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The pre-existing resume blocks the first post-switch turn and ensures the new prompt/tool profile is applied.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue post-switch model requests with the resumed session's prompt and enabled tools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing agent-loop request count; the first and later HydraFusion requests carry fewer tool schemas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The restart occurred, but the rebuilt session retained the generic full tool inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the turn critical path; payload decreases while using HydraFusion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scales with user model-boundary switches, not workspace size. Request payload savings scale with post-switch turns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model changes and sends are serialized by the existing per-chat sequencer. Restart/resume is one-at-a-time; the diff adds no burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Restart rebuilds authoritative session config once; subsequent turns reuse the SDK session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for exact HydraFusion IDs. Family-aliased preview IDs do not use the exact-ID restart check, but that is a missed optimization/correctness consideration rather than a diff-introduced performance regression because their prior tool payload was already full.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Boundary-switch frequency varies, but restart cardinality is unchanged and the profile reduction is direct.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; expensive restart behavior predates the diff and the changed profile reduces subsequent request payload.

Scenarios.Scenario: Launch a non-HydraFusion session or a HydraFusion session with an explicit tool filter
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session config construction and SDK create/resume remain the critical path. The model check returns no default for other families, and either configured filter suppresses the default for HydraFusion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or resume the SDK session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One normal-path RPC per launch/resume, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK RPC received the user-configured filters or no filters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks readiness; changed synchronous branching is negligible and adds no boundary call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send model requests using the resulting explicit or generic tool profile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing requests per turn; no changed fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent tool filters and request cardinality were used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Explicit user filter behavior and non-Hydra request payloads are preserved.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Bounded by override pattern count and current client-tool count; the PR adds only one constant-time family comparison when the default is not used.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged existing parallel config preparation and one normal-path SDK launch RPC.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache change. Override resolution still reads in-memory configuration once per launch/resume.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the guard requiring both filters to be undefined and exact family matching.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; overhead is bounded synchronous work with no new boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host module startup and prompt contributor registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Importing allPrompts now imports the HydraFusion contributor, constructs two small fixed strings, and registers one class before sessions can resolve prompts.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant one-time work independent of sessions, workspace size, or history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single module initialization; no queue, task, or background work is started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The strings and registry entry are retained for process lifetime but have fixed, tiny cardinality and are reused by all HydraFusion launches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from static module initialization and singleton registry ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Negligible bounded allocation; no external boundary or repeated construction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup or retention regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and traced session launch/resume, model switching, tool registration/filtering, prompt assembly, runtime RPC, filesystem setup, and repeated model-request payloads. No diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold. The PR fixes a concrete repeated tool-schema serialization/network-cost regression for HydraFusion, which was recorded with its introducing commit.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
